source.title: Combining Adam and its Inverse Counterpart to Enhance Generalization of Deep Learning Optimizers
source.authors: Tao Shi; Liang-Ming Chen; Longjie Jin; Meng-Chu Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table content is flattened, and the cited Supplementary File is not included.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer training outcomes using test accuracy and validation perplexity/generalization gap, bearing on optimizer-dependent generalization in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and generalization measurements. Its cited prior-work descriptions are not treated as results. It does not directly compare standalone SGD with adaptive optimizers.
record.test_reason: The Adam-versus-SWATS comparisons test V4's switching-to-SGD recovery component, and Adam-versus-AdamW comparisons bear on its decoupled-weight-decay component. Comparisons against the proposed DualAdam alone do not test V4. No standalone SGD baseline establishes the central adaptive-versus-SGD claim or full recovery of that gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that InvAdam improves escape from sharp minima but can fail to converge, and that a linear transition from InvAdam to Adam balances exploration and convergence. They report better generalization for DualAdam than Adam and tested variants on image classification and LLM fine-tuning. These conclusions do not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer generalization in image classification and LLM fine-tuning, but does not test the original V4 SGD comparisons or its limited-tuning setup; introduces DualAdam as the principal intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across optimizer, model, and dataset; the switching-rate ablation reports that too small or too large a rate degrades performance, and InvAdam alone may not converge.

fits_no_version.finding: DualAdam outperforms Adam and the tested variants on the reported image-classification benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An early InvAdam phase followed by a linear transition to Adam can improve image-classification accuracy over the tested Adam-family recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: In OpenPangu-Embedded-1B fine-tuning, AdamW achieves lower training loss, while DualAdam has lower, more stable validation perplexity and a near-zero reported loss gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DualAdam can reduce overfitting relative to AdamW in the tested instruction-fine-tuning setting.

fits_no_version.finding: DualAdam has smaller Hessian eigenvalues and trace than Adam on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, and a flatter Gaussian-direction loss profile on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested DualAdam solutions are flatter under Hessian and unscaled random-direction diagnostics; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware gap-ranking claim.

record.problems: No standalone SGD comparison for V4. ImageNet-1k table omits uncertainty; LLM values are figure-only. The switching-rate ablation table is flattened and contains an apparent misalignment between stated metrics and entries.
record.rows_left_out: Table I also reports AdamW, NAdam, RAdam, Adan, and MIAdam for each model and dataset; omitted to stay within 60 rows while retaining Adam, SWATS, and DualAdam comparisons. Table II reports Tiny ImageNet results, but its flattened layout does not reliably associate all values with subjects and optimizers; omitted rather than reconstructing assignments. Other optimizer rows are omitted for the same row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance under random labels.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Standalone adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons; the limited-tuning premise; equal or better training performance in those comparisons; broader tuning; recovery to standalone SGD performance; word-level language-model comparisons. AdamW comparisons do not isolate weight-decay implementation from other recipe choices because detailed settings are in the unavailable supplement.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's blanket image-classification support label and its LLM limits_scope label. V4 verdicts concern only the switching and decoupled-weight-decay components. Tiny ImageNet is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing; Table II also shows SWATS below Adam for all three models. Figure-only reporting is not itself evidence of a scope limitation. Reported means and standard deviations do not establish statistical significance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
No standalone SGD baseline; broader hyperparameter tuning, word-level language models, and the stated weight-decay/switching recovery conditions are not tested.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
